causal_chain: 14:12:00 chg-4417 begins a 3-stage canary on checkout-api (d-08 5%, d-09 25% at 14:16, d-10 100% at 14:20). One diff moves five outbound-client keys: http.client.max_retries 2->5, backoff exp_jitter->fixed_50ms, retry_budget_pct 10->disabled, max_inflight 32->unlimited, pool.max_idle 8->16.

14:12:03 the rollout-start line (l-05) is the last clean record on any plane; 55s later checkout-api emits the first anomaly anywhere (l-06, 'attempt=3/5'). Both lines are checkout-api, i.e. one host clock, so no clock offset can invert them. Arithmetic on the fixed 50ms backoff bounds attempt 1 of that burst to ~14:12:57.8, worst case 14:12:51.9 - still after 14:12:03.

Canary instances begin issuing up to 5 attempts per logical pricing.quote call instead of 2, with no retry budget to throttle them. Traces fingerprint this directly: a sick request with items=1 spawns FIVE sequential children, all carrying ONE idempotency key with attempt=1,2,3,4,5 (t-12..t-16) - literal repetition of one logical call, versus the healthy pattern of one child per SKU with distinct keys (t-03/t-04/t-05).

Outbound volume rises with inbound demand flat: checkout rps_out 1132->1290 while rps_in holds 948->951 (m-checkout-api-03 vs -04), and edge/checkout ingress stays flat in all 11 buckets. This is a change in per-request behaviour, not in traffic.

The amplification scales with canary DOSE, not with downstream errors. Inverting the mix model gives an implied changed-fraction of 0.035 / 0.331 / 0.849 / 0.963 against the scheduled 0.05 / 0.25 / 1.00 / 1.00 (m-checkout-api-04..-07). At the first deviating bucket the extra calls (+158 rps) exceed pricing's total errors (~3.9/s) by ~40x, so the initial increment is unconditional, not error-triggered.

Because max_inflight was simultaneously removed (32->unlimited), the retry demand from a small canary fraction was not bounded to that fraction: pricing-svc pool occupancy roughly doubles from 15/48 (l-02, baseline) to 31/48 within ~2 minutes (l-07, 14:14:30), while pricing-svc itself had shipped no change for 46 hours (d-02 to d-15).

The amplified attempt volume saturates a fixed 48-slot connection pool attested independently by metrics (m-pricing-svc-06 first 48/48 at 14:24, pool_max=48 in all 11 records, never resized) and by pricing-svc's own logs (l-10, l-13, l-17, l-22, l-30, l-36, l-40: 'no connection available in_use=48 max=48', waited_ms rising 812->2411).

Connection acquisition, not work, becomes the cost: pool_wait_ms is 94-98% of every sick pricing span (t-12..t-15 380/430/470/500; t-20/t-21 580/590) and residual non-wait work is only 12-28ms, BELOW the healthy 57-61ms end-to-end. Attempts terminate in pool_timeout=true (t-16, t-22). This is a traces-plane measurement, corroborated in kind - not in value - by pricing's pool gauge and PoolTimeout logs.

Failed and abandoned attempts feed more attempts, so the multiplier climbs 1.356 -> 2.765 -> 5.231 -> 5.772 and then SATURATES at the configured ceiling: 5.772 is 97.0% of baseline fanout 1.19 x 5 attempts = 5.95. It is a bounded multiplier pinned to the deployed parameter, and it plateaus while pricing's error rate is still rising (0.243->0.261), so it is not tracking downstream errors.

Pricing-svc collapses under the manufactured load: queue full and load shed at depth=512 (l-27), p99 4400ms, error_rate 0.261, saturation 0.98 (m-pricing-svc-08); checkout-api reports 'inflight=214 limit=unlimited' (l-18), 'retry budget disabled; not throttling retries' (l-29) and fanout=5.76 (l-44); pricing confirms duplicate work server-side with 'duplicate request detected ... seen=4/seen=5' (l-20, l-33). edge-gateway is a pure pass-through victim, emitting 502/504s that blame checkout-api (l-19, l-28, l-39) with its own fanout flat at 0.795-0.799.

14:44:08 chg-4423 reverts chg-4417 (d-14, l-46); 14:44:51 the retry keys are restored (l-47 'max_retries=2 backoff=exp_jitter retry_budget_pct=10'). Pricing's pool drains 81 seconds later at UNCHANGED capacity (l-48 'pool recovered in_use=27 max=48'), edge is healthy by 14:48:03 (l-49), and only then is capacity added at 14:52:07 (l-51, d-15 replicas 12->20) - 5m55s AFTER recovery. Demand-side reversal was sufficient; capacity was irrelevant. Full baseline at 14:56 (m-*-11), with the retry ceiling observed back at 1/2 (l-52, t-25).
ruled_out: chg-4420 (auth-svc, jwt.cache.key sub->sub+aud, ttl_s 60->900, 14:31) - the most seductive decoy, since an audience-blind cache key is exactly the shape of cache_key_collision. Dead on ordering: it POSTDATES the first anomaly by 18 minutes, the first metrics deviation by 15, and the first PoolTimeout by 13. Dead on symptoms: auth-svc shows zero latency, error, load or pool deviation in all 11 buckets (m-auth-svc-01..-11) and logs only healthy lines (l-24, l-35, l-42). Dead on recovery: it was NEVER reverted, yet full baseline was reached at 14:56. Its one real footprint - hit ratio 0.91->0.96->0.97 first moving at 14:44 and never reverting - is an effect of its own 15x TTL extension, not of the incident.

cache_key_collision as a mechanism - rejected across three planes. No change in the entire 4-day inventory ever altered cart-store's key format; the only key-format change (chg-4420) is the ineligible decoy above. Logs show zero plane-wide matches for 'stale' and no line anywhere shows a wrong or mismatched value served. cart-store first deviates at 14:16, the SAME bucket as everything else and never earlier, never emitted a single ERROR, was never blamed by any service, and recovered to 0.94 with no change of its own. Residual unexplained oddity I could not close: one healthy post-incident span (t-28) reads another trace's key cart:v2:8842 and gets a HIT; spans carry no payload, so correctness is unverifiable.

cart-store's 2.58x inbound growth with hit ratio falling 0.94->0.70 - the strongest quantitative objection to my verdict, since retried IDENTICAL reads should raise a hit ratio, not lower it. Resolved without a new cause: pricing.quote is a LEAF span with uninstrumented children and pricing-svc has NO rps_out metric on any record, so the pricing->cart-store edge is invisible rather than absent, and cart's growth (2.58x) sits below pricing's intake growth (4.87x) as a partial downstream share would. Falling hit ratio needs no novel keys: requests abandoned mid-flight on pool_timeout never complete their cache write-back, and eviction churn (evictions_5m=41200, l-21) plus widened miss windows do the rest. Honest caveat: that edge is inferred from a coefficient fit, never directly observed.

chg-4413 (cart-store, cache.max_entries 200k->260k, 09:31) - eligible on timing but dead on dose and recovery: it was at 100% for five hours before onset, so it cannot produce a step change at 14:12, it was never reverted while the fleet fully recovered, and cart-store never led any deviation.

chg-4415 (edge-gateway, tls.session_cache 8192->16384, 14:02, WITH an unexamined version bump) - the most dangerous predating decoy, landing 10 minutes before chg-4417 with unverified code. Dead on dose-invariance: it was at 100% before onset. Dead on symptoms: edge rps_in (1180-1204) and edge fanout (0.795-0.799) are flat in ALL 11 buckets, so the edge tier neither amplified nor retried; edge shows no distress until 14:20:33 (l-12), 18 minutes after its own deploy, and only ever blames checkout-api. Never reverted, yet recovery completed.

chg-4408 (checkout-api, feature.flag.split_ship on, 07-27) and n_plus_one_fanout - the flag genuinely multiplies per-request downstream calls, and it was live through the incident. Dead as generator on three planes: traces show baseline children track item count EXACTLY with distinct keys and SKUs (items=3->3, items=2->2, items=1->1), while both sick traces have items=1 yet 5 and 3 children ALL sharing one idem key with attempt=1..N - repetition, not per-item work. Per-tier counts are 1->1->5->0 with multiplication at exactly ONE tier; there is no 1->3->9 cascade. Metrics show demand flat in all 11 buckets, so the item mix cannot have shifted. Decisively, the flag was at 100% for 27 hours before onset and was never reverted while the fleet recovered - it is dose-invariant. It survives only as a possible multiplicand that retries amplified.

connection_pool_exhaustion - real, directly logged, and the proximate cause of the user-visible errors, but a CONSEQUENCE, not the trigger. Ordering: checkout's egress rose at 14:16 while pricing's pool was still only 19/48; the pool did not pin at 48/48 until 14:24. Capacity: pool_max=48 is constant in all 11 metrics records and in every log line including recovery - nothing shrank it, and no change in the inventory ever altered a pricing-svc pool. Agency: pricing-svc shipped nothing for 46 hours. Recovery: the pool drained at UNCHANGED max=48 within 81s of the retry-key restore and 5m55s before any replica was added. Note the diff RAISED pool.max_idle 8->16, i.e. more idle retention, which relieves rather than causes pressure.

unbounded_concurrency - the closest rival and the one I cannot fully separate, since max_inflight 32->unlimited shipped in the SAME diff, on the same canary ladder, with the same single rollback. Demoted to permissive co-factor, not generator, on two grounds no other reading explains: (1) removing an in-flight ceiling cannot mint an attempt DENOMINATOR of 5 - logs show the ceiling moving 1/2 -> x/5 -> restored 2 -> 1/2 (l-01, l-06/l-14, l-47, l-52), traces show attempt=1..5 on ONE idem key, and the metrics plateau sits at 97% of exactly 5x baseline; (2) traces show sibling spans strictly SEQUENTIAL with zero overlap, so per-request parallelism is 1. 'inflight=214' (l-18) is not independent support for the concurrency limb - it is rate x inflated latency, a consequence. I record it as the enabling co-factor that let a 5% canary saturate a shared pool.

clock_skew - measured but non-causal. clock_offset_ms=-118 appears on exactly ONE host (pricing-svc-7) with the IDENTICAL value in a healthy pre-incident span (t-09, 13:52), the sick span (t-12, 14:20) and a healthy post-incident span (t-26, 14:56): zero drift, no correlation with failure, and every other slow span carries no offset at all. A constant offset contributes 0ms to any duration since start and end are read from the same clock, and 118ms is 4.7% of a 2501ms symptom. Logs have zero plane-wide matches for clock/NTP/skew/drift/not-yet-valid/expired, and the decisive ordering pair (l-05 vs l-06) is intra-service on one clock. Where skew IS load-bearing: it corrupts my backoff fingerprint on the one offset host - the first inter-attempt gap is 146ms raw but 28ms skew-corrected, BELOW the 50ms floor, so I rest that fingerprint only on the three clean gaps (51/52/52ms) on non-offset hosts plus 50/50ms in the second sick trace. Two earlier log 'inversions' were withdrawn by the logs plane itself in favour of idempotency-key reuse across request waves, which is intra-service arithmetic no constant offset can produce.

chg-4421 (edge-gateway, upstream.timeout_ms 1500->2500, 14:34) - postdates the first anomaly by 21 minutes; ineligible. Flagged separately as an effect-precedes-cause anomaly in the evidence itself: a 504 with dur_ms=2501 was already logged at 14:22:47 (l-19), 11m22s BEFORE the 2500ms ceiling was announced (l-38), so the recorded diff cannot explain the ceiling that was already in force. Annotated 'no effect' and never reverted.

chg-4425 (pricing-svc, replicas 12->20, 14:52) - the intuitive 'we were under-provisioned' story, and doubly ineligible: it postdates onset by 37 minutes AND postdates measured recovery (pool recovered 14:46:12, edge healthy 14:48:03). Capacity was added to an already-healed system.

chg-4419 (cart-store, trace.sampling 0.10->0.25, 14:26) - postdates cart-store's own first deviation (14:16 bucket) by ~10 minutes, by which time the cache slide was already three buckets deep. Telemetry-only, but it does mean raw span volume is not comparable across 14:26, which I accounted for by reasoning from per-trace SHAPE (children per request, idem keys, attempt counters) rather than span counts.
